Commentary.Commentary: We are back.
..SECOND INNINGS...

Zimbabwe won't be much disappointed though. They bowled well, Blessing Muzarabani in particular who scalped 7 wickets and rattled through the Irish line up. He was well supported by the others. Just the could of big partnership has taken a bit of game away from them. They would have loved to tumble the opposition for a much lower total and they were ein a good position to do the job as well but credit to McBrine and Adair. Now, Zimbabwe more than hour to play with the bat, they'll hope to end the day without losing any wickets. Can they? Let's find out.

So, McBrine is stranded on 90 as he loses all his partners. He has single handedly taken his team over 250. McBrine walked in when Zimbabwe were in a nervous position. They were 82/6 at one stage and asking for a partnership. Lorcan Tucker played a handy attacking innings but fell but then came the big much needed stand between Adair and McBrine. The duo added 120 odd runs to take Ireland to a competitive total. Adair fell after a well made 78 but McBrine along with the tail played brilliantly, he would have loved a ton but more importantly has helped Ireland in a big way.

...DAY 1, THIRD SESSION...

A fine session for the visitors as they have scored plenty of runs but in the last 15 minutes or so lost a couple of wickets. They started the session with Andy McBrine and Mark Adair trying to steady the ship. McBrine was watchful throughout his innings but Adair played with intent and made the hosts think a lot. He scored plenty of boundaries and scored a quick fifty. He fell and Barry McCarthy followed him. Ireland still have McBrine and will hope he can push them around 250. Zimbabwe have relied on Blessing Muzarabani so far who has taken six wickets and will hope the tall right hander will clean the tail up quickly. Join us for the final session soon.
Short in length and on off, Craig Young ducks but the ball stays low and he gets hit on the helmet. TEA!

....Day 1, Session 2...

An entertaining start to the game. Zimbabwe will be the happier side though as they have scalped six wickets with Blessing Muzarabani topping the chart with four wickets. He rattled the Irish top order and gave no breathing space. Andy McBrine and Lorcan Tucker did stitched a fine fifty runs partnership but the latter fell to Trevor Gwandu. He was looking really good for his 33 runs but perished. Ireland are now into the lower batting order. McBrine has looked solid so far but need help from others. Zimbabwe on the other hand will hope their pacers could extra bounce from the pitch and clean up the Irish batters quickly. Stay tuned for the second session.
Flat and outside off, angling in. McBrine pads it away. LUNCH.
